question: Which of the following is a cause of pollution of water resources?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Radioactive substances.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Radioactive waste **is a source of **water pollution**.
 
• **Radioactive substances** are used in **nuclear power plants**, **industrial, medical, **and** other scientific processes.**
 
• They can be found in watches, luminous clocks, television sets, and x-ray machinery.
 
• There are also naturally occurring radioisotopes from organisms and within the environment. If not properly disposed of, **radioactive waste can result in serious water pollution incidents.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• There are two sources of radioactive contamination in drinking water.
 
 
• The first is naturally occurring radionuclides that are contained in the soil that water moves through. Some areas are susceptible to contamination from phosphate-rich soils and rock.
 
• The second source of radioactive contamination comes from man-made sources.
 
 
 
• Radionuclides found in drinking water are members of three radioactive series, uranium, thorium, and actinium, and include the naturally occurring elements radium, uranium, and the radioactive gas radon. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deforestation: **

 
 
• ​Deforestation is the **permanent removal of trees** or a decrease in the forest area to make room for something besides the forest.
 
• **Forests cover more than 30%** of the **Earth's land surface**, according to the World Wildlife Fund.
